transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE); Olivia Chen (Redwood SE); Ethan Ross (Mittelbank Procurement); Leila Haddad (Mittelbank Legal); Marco Alvarez (Mittelbank CTO); Nora Kim (Mittelbank Security)

Summary: Quick procurement + legal preflight for pilot. Customer wants clarity on SLA crediting, DPA subprocessors, KMS options, and whether Dedicated vs Private makes more sense for low-latency payments flow. AE/SE pair aligned to send redlines, perf script and pricing spreadsheet.

Topics: pricing approvals, MSA redlines, DPA entitlements, SLA burn / credits, private deployment options (VPC/on-prem), KMS & SSO, pilot acceptance criteria, benchmarking plan

-- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, auto-generated transcript; occasional errors) --
00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — let's, uh, do intros real quick. I'm Samir, AE at Redwood. Olivia — will you intro?
00:12 Olivia: Hi team, Olivia Chen, solutions engineer. I'll run the technical bits and the pilot benchmarks.
00:18 Ethan: Ethan Ross, procurement. We've got Leila on legal, Marco on infra and Nora on security.
00:25 Leila: Hi, thanks.
00:28 Marco: Hi all.
00:32 Nora: Good to be here.
01:05 Samir: Goal for today — surface any procurement blockers, get alignment on what the legal asks are for the DPA/MSA, and scope the pilot acceptance criteria so finance can sign off. Also talk pricing path.
02:03 Ethan: Quick context — Mittelbank is evaluating for payments fraud detection in prod. Latency is sensitive, cost is obviously a factor, and we need clear SLA behaviour for transaction scoring path. We also have strict residency and subprocessor requirements.
03:20 Olivia: From a tech perspective we recommend starting hosted pilot but variant for dedicated capacity if predictable qps and low p50/p95 are required. We can also run Private (VPC) for full control — just higher ops/approval.
04:02 Leila: On the DPA side we need list of subprocessors, standard SCCs — and any options for not using third-party keying, i.e., bring-your-own-KMS. We also look for audit logs retention windows.
04:45 Samir: Sure — we'll share a subprocessors list. BYOK / KMS is supported in Redwood Private, and we have an SSO/KMS integration playbook, Olivia will follow up.
05:30 Marco: How realistic is low-latency on hosted versus dedicated? If we do hosted, what's fallback to a lower-cost model — does it increase tail latency?
06:10 Olivia: There's a tradeoff. Hosted gives fastest onboard but multi-tenant variability. Dedicated = pinned GPU pools, predictable throughput. For p95 SLOs we recommend dedicated for production. For pilot you can use hosted with burst capacity or reserved dedicated for the short window.
07:00 Ethan: Pricing committee needs a breakdown: per-token vs per-inference, plus any reserved capacity minimums. Also egress fees if we do cross-region.
07:32 Samir: We'll share an itemized spreadsheet. Pilot pricing can be arranged as time-limited credits or trial discount, then we map committed monthly usage for Dedicated.
08:10 Leila: On SLA credits — we need a clear definition of downtime, partial degradations, and the credit formula. Also acceptance tests for the pilot influence SLA start.
09:05 Olivia: We have standard SLA language: uptime and latency SLOs with credits pro-rated. For partial degradation (e.g., increased p95) we propose a graduated credit band. We can sketch a concrete table.
09:40 Nora: Security Qs — do you retain input data? How long, and is there a redaction option? Where are audit logs stored?
10:05 Samir: By default, hosted stores minimal logs for X days but we can change retention and ACLs in Private. We support configurable retention and can disable retention for sensitive flows. We'll put exact retention defaults in the security pack.
10:45 Leila: On subprocessors — need to know if any third-party eval services or vector DBs are used.
11:10 Olivia: For embeddings and storage we support customer-managed vector stores but hosted options may use partner services; we'll list them.
11:45 Ethan: Also curious about escrow and data export timelines — if we decide to terminate, what's the data handoff?
12:12 Samir: Standard export within 30 days, plus a documented process for deletion. We'll put that in the MSA addendum.
13:01 (crosstalk) Marco: — the KV cache, is that persisted? Olivia: KV cache is ephemeral per node but, uh, we can snapshot for warm starts — apologies if that explanation was fuzzy.
14:02 Olivia: For pilot acceptance, we propose: stability for two weeks at expected qps, p99 under X ms (we'll propose numbers), no security findings above medium, and successful SSO/KMS integration.
15:10 Ethan: Sounds good. Procurement needs exact numbers by next review meeting.
16:22 Leila: On DPA exceptions — we might need to limit subprocessors list, and also require contractual language for audit rights. There's a specific compliance team that wants audit windows.
17:05 Samir: We can include audit rights and SOC 2 type II attestations; we also have FedRAMP pathway docs but not certified yet — we'll clarify.
18:30 Nora: KMS flow — do we support customer HSMs or only cloud KMS?
18:48 Olivia: We support cloud KMS integrations and in Private deployments you can point at your HSM/KMS endpoints. There's some ops work.
19:22 Marco: If we run Private in our VPC, what maintenance windows and upgrades look like? We need an upgrade SLA and rollback plan.
20:00 Samir: For Private we map maintenance windows with customers; upgrades can be scheduled with a canary rollout and rollback. We'll include an ops runbook in the handoff.
21:07 Ethan: Pricing committee also worried about a minimum committed spend for Dedicated. If the pilot doesn't reach that, what's the conversion path?
21:45 Samir: We can offer a pilot credit and then propose tiered reserved capacity commitments tied to discounts. We'll surface conversion economics.
22:30 Leila: Regarding DPA items, we might need specific clauses for data residency in EU. Are you able to restrict hosting region?
23:01 Olivia: Yes, we have region pinning and can route requests to EU-only clusters; Private gives you total control.
23:40 Nora: Encryption in transit and at rest details? TLS version, perfect forward secrecy?
24:05 Olivia: We use modern TLS with PFS, and at-rest encryption is AES-256. We'll detail cipher suites in the security pack; apologies if I mumbled the exact string earlier.
25:12 Marco: Any third-party dependencies for logs or traces?
25:33 Samir: We use partners for optional observability if customers enable; by default Redwood Console stores traces in our platform but customers can export.
26:10 (small pause)
26:40 Leila: For the MSA redlines — we will propose a few non-standard clauses: stronger indemnity carveouts for us, and more restrictive subprocessors list. Would you be open to narrowing that?
27:05 Samir: We can be flexible on subprocessors; indemnity we usually negotiate case-by-case. We'll flag legal to take a look and give a response in the redline.
28:00 Ethan: Can you provide a sample SLA credit formula now, even rough?
28:22 Olivia: Roughly: if monthly uptime < 99.5%, 10% credit; < 99% 25% credit; sustained latency p95 above SLO gives smaller credits. We'll write a table.
29:10 Samir: We'll propose a table and include sample pilot SLOs.
30:00 Marco: For acceptance tests, we want the ability to run our synthetic workload against your hosted infra — can we get a bench harness?
30:25 Olivia: Yes — we'll share a benchmark harness and scripts. We'll also include sample traces and guidance on KV cache sizing.
31:00 Nora: Security assessment — can we schedule a short architecture review with your security lead?
31:20 Samir: Yes, we can set a security deep-dive with our security PM; Olivia will coordinate.
32:10 Leila: A quick note on DPA: we may need to restrict transfer outside EEA for the payments data unless explicit consent.
32:40 Olivia: Noted — region pinning and Private deployment are the ways to meet that.
33:30 (audio glitch)
34:10 Ethan: Timeline — procurement committee meets next Friday. If we can get redlines and pricing by Thu EOD we can route to them.
34:35 Samir: We'll aim for Thu EOD for the doc pack.
35:12 Olivia: I'll also attach the pilot performance script and a suggested config for KV cache and batching.
36:00 Marco: One last thing — what's the rollback for a model regression? If quantized model causes quality hit, do you have version pinning and fallback?
36:30 Olivia: Yes — model pinning and automatic fallback policies are supported. We'll include the rollout and canary strategy in the rollout section.
37:12 Leila: On audit logs — we need 12 months retention for some telemetry. Is that possible for logs?
37:40 Samir: Yes we can extend retention as an add-on. We'll note retention tiers.
38:20 Nora: Any certifications you can share? SOC2, ISO27001?
38:35 Samir: SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA; ISO is in progress. We'll share SOC2 once NDA is in place.
39:10 (background voice: yep)
39:45 Ethan: Ok, that covers my procurement checklist mostly. We'll need cost sensitivity to inflight traffic spikes — is there a burst pricing model?
40:10 Samir: We have burst capacity for Dedicated and burst billing for hosted — details in pricing sheet.
41:00 Olivia: Also note caching and batching recommendations can reduce token cost by ~20-40% for typical seq lengths; we'll include a modeling example.
41:45 Marco: Good. Next steps recap?
42:05 Samir: Quick recap: Samir send MSA redlines and pricing spreadsheet by Thu (2025-03-14). Olivia send bench harness, perf targets, KV cache config by Tue (2025-03-18). Schedule security deep-dive with Redwood security PM — target next week. Mittelbank legal to send DPA clause list for escalation by 2025-03-19. Marco confirm deployment appetite by 2025-03-20.
43:00 Leila: That timeline works.
43:12 Nora: We'll aim to prep our SSO details.
44:00 (small talk, table clearing)
45:10 Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in writing with links to the security pack, pilot pricing spreadsheet, and the benchmark script.
46:00 Ethan: Appreciate it.
46:20 Marco: Thanks.
46:40 (meeting adjourns)

References shared during call: "pilot-pricing-v1.xlsx" (Samir to send), "redwood-security-pack.pdf" (link forthcoming), "bench-harness.zip" (Olivia to share), draft MSA redline (Samir)

End of transcript.
